experimental_method: Synthetic method in a variable-volume high-pressure autoclave with sapphire window, magnetic stirrer and electrodes: weighed NaCl (or CaCl2) solution plus weighed CH4 heated slowly (3-6 K/min) at constant volume; phase-boundary points from break points of the P-T isochores, confirmed visually and by the electrolytic resistance between two vertically mounted electrodes.
uncertainties_stated: Pressure: maximum uncertainty 0.8 % at 30 MPa to 0.1 % at 300 MPa. Temperature: inhomogeneities along the autoclave not above 0.2 K. Salt solution amounts +/-0.1 %; CH4 amounts up to 0.4 % at small concentrations; sample volume 0.3-0.4 %. Molar volume: e.g. at 723 K, 100 MPa, 12.6 mol% CH4, 0.16 mol% NaCl, maximum error 1.2 %, most probable 0.7 %; up to 1.5 % at a few tens of MPa and at the highest pressures.
quality_remarks: Points lie on the fluid-fluid phase boundary surface near the critical region (630-800 K, 40-265 MPa); they are homogenisation points of mixtures of known overall composition, not coexisting-phase compositions. Temperatures printed to 1 K. The Table 3 compositions correspond to about 8.6-8.7 wt% NaCl relative to water although the text says 8 wt%. Above about 70 mol% CH4 salt precipitates (no data there). Table 4 is interpolated. Binary H2O-CH4 isopleths of this work (16.8 and 62.9 mol% CH4) are shown only in Figs. 1-3; supercritical PVT isochor data are only referenced to the thesis [5].

All four tables were therefore transcribed completely from the page images (250 dpi, problem cells at 500 dpi) and then diffed number-by-number against the OCR text layer; every disagreement is listed in changes_after_image_check. Layout: in each isopleth the three species mol% values are printed beside the first three data rows; each is written as one label row ('H2O 87.19 CH4 12.65 NaCl 0.160') followed by the data rows (v2.1 rule 10), and group_rows set composition.constant.H2O / CH4 / NaCl (or CaCl2) in mol%. Row indices 0-based after the header, label rows included. Checks: every block's mol% sum is 100.00 +/- 0.005; wt% NaCl relative to water from the mol% = 0.57-0.60 (Table 1), 1.69-1.73 (Table 2), 8.6-8.7 (Table 3); CaCl2 0.52, 1.6, 6.4 wt%. Molar volume V decreases monotonically along every isopleth (checked); P rises along every isopleth except Table 1 row 2 (44.7 -> 44.6 MPa) and Table 2 row 9 (47.0 -> 46.5 MPa), both as printed (the text notes flat pressure minima at low salt and low CH4). Property set to 'other' (phase-boundary isopleth with molar volume); see the mapping's property_description.
